nodes.label: Bearing Block Model
nodes.rationale: The orbitable 3D split plummer/pillow block is the lesson subject because it yields all four BIS line types in one view and makes visible edges become hidden edges as it spins; the body no longer redraws the full base slab to avoid non-manifold 'spiderweb' edges and false occlusion.

nodes.label: Hidden-Line Occlusion Raycaster
nodes.rationale: The CPU line-of-sight occlusion raycaster (accelerated by three-mesh-bvh) is REQUIRED, not an optimisation: it makes the visible-Type-A vs hidden-Type-E/F decision that produces dashed lines, the topic's whole reason to exist. Phase 3 tried to drop it for a GPU depth-buffer X-ray and broke the lesson; it was reverted (ADR-029 addendum / ADR-030). Runs live per rAF on orbit.

nodes.label: Front View Projection Morph
nodes.rationale: A dual-camera projectionMorphK matrix blend eases perspective to orthographic so the Front View lands on a true parallel elevation with no 'pop'; dragging or scrolling out eases smoothly back to free-orbit 3D via a single guarded morph so a continued gesture can't fight it.

nodes.label: Line Classification Fixes
nodes.rationale: Math/classification-layer fixes in lineDrawer.js: a coplanar-coverage flush-seam filter drops the false body/foot seam, edge subdivision into ~0.5-unit sub-segments lets a long arris draw solid then dashed exactly where it leaves view, and negating buried contact-face normals stops genuine creases self-occluding while orbiting.

nodes.label: BIS Line-Type Stepper
nodes.rationale: Four-step guided reveal (Type A / Type E-F / Type G / Type B) driven by foundationSteps.js; adds strict BIS 3:1 solid-filled arrowheads, an Aligned vs Unidirectional dimension-text toggle, and an 'Inspect arrowhead' micro-zoom, so completion latches the moment Type B dimensions are revealed.

nodes.label: Quiet Chrome Scrollbar (Foundations)
nodes.rationale: The step-card scroll region shows a floating padded pill tinted to --color-border (ADR-032 Quiet Chrome) instead of a hidden scrollbar, giving a 'more content below' cue; scrollbar-width stays unset on the base rule so Chrome 121+ keeps the WebKit pseudo-elements.
